name: Tiara Apartments
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: KCG Development plans to buy and rehabilitate Tiara Apartments, a 50-unit 1962 Section 8 building for adults 62 and older at 12000 E. 16th Avenue next to the Anschutz Medical Campus in Aurora, at about $140,000 per unit; it won 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits from CHFA, with $10.3M of CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: It is a preservation deal for an expiring Section 8 Moderate Rehabilitation contract that the owner had been marketing to market-rate buyers; the plan converts it through RAD to a new 20-year project-based contract, but no public record shows the purchase or rehab has happened.

status.label: Credits awarded; acquisition and rehab start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA reserved the credits in November 2024. The application targeted a financial closing in the first half of 2025, within 90 days of the award, followed by construction; no public record of a sale, bond closing, RAD conversion, permit or start of rehab was found.

next_step: Watch for an Adams County deed transferring 12000 E. 16th Avenue to a KCG entity, a CHFA bond closing, a HUD RAD conversion record and a City of Aurora minor site plan amendment or building permit.

key_numbers.value: 50 homes for adults 62+, all with rental assistance
key_numbers.meaning: 9 studios, 23 one-bedroom and 18 two-bedroom units at 30%, 50% and 60% AMI, all covered by a HAP contract.
About $8.8M over 10 years, plus $1,330,000 of accelerated state credit.
Privately placed tax-exempt construction bonds; $6.09M permanent bonds and a taxable construction loan of about $4.55M per the application.

key_numbers.value: Over $7M of hard-cost rehab (about $140,000 per unit)
key_numbers.meaning: First substantial renovation since 1983: new elevator, building systems, air conditioning, envelope, ADA and vapor mitigation, with residents temporarily relocated.

facts.value: One five-story building with a single elevator, built in 1962; last renovated in 1983; never had tax credits
HAP contract on 100% of units under the Section 8 Moderate Rehabilitation program, expiring in 2025; to be converted through RAD to a new 20-year Project-Based Rental Assistance contract
Elderly and disabled residents; historically 100% occupied
Qualified Census Tract, one block from the Fitzsimons/Anschutz Medical Campus; two bus stops within 0.1 mile, light rail about 1 mile
Purchase and sale agreement dated February 2024, conditioned on a tax credit award; seller and price not public

Aurora Housing Authority stated its intent to be special limited partner, giving a property tax exemption (about $60,000 a year, adding about $710,000 of borrowing capacity) and a permit fee waiver worth over $25,000

Phase I flagged a former dry cleaner on the east adjoining property; Phase II found indoor vapor levels above EPA thresholds, so a vapor mitigation system is budgeted along with asbestos and lead paint abatement
A minor amendment to the site plan, which the applicant expected to fit within a 90-day closing timeline
Because rents stay 100% subsidized, the study tested households at or below 30% AMI (41.1% income eligible); surveyed affordable properties average 98.9% occupancy

money.source: Colorado accelerated state housing tax credit
money.note: The applicant asked for a waiver of the state credit applicable percentage rate; the QCT location covers what it says would otherwise be a federal equity gap of over $1.4M.
Construction-period bonds, private placement; permanent bonds $6,090,000; taxable construction loan about $4,550,000 (application).

money.source: Capital Magnet Fund loan (Impact Development Fund)
money.note: KCG intended to apply; no award record found.

money.source: Aurora Housing Authority partnership (tax exemption and permit fee waiver)
money.amount: About $60,000 a year in property tax; over $25,000 in permit fees

parties.name: KCG Development, LLC (Tiara would be its first Colorado project)

parties.role: Tax credit consultant; green consultant; environmental consultant
parties.name: S.B. Clark Companies; Group 14; PSI

background.text: The current owner had been marketing the property to market-rate investors and developers before KCG put it under contract in February 2024, conditioned on a tax credit award; the seller's name and price are not in the public application.

Rehab scope: all 50 unit interiors (kitchens and bathrooms), roofs, windows, siding and balconies, boilers, water heaters, electrical and plumbing, new air conditioning, a full elevator replacement, partial electrification, low-flow fixtures, four units upgraded for ADA plus accessible paths, cameras, lighting and perimeter fencing, a gazebo and expanded gardens.
The temporary relocation budget is over $500,000, including hotel stays, because of the single elevator and the abatement work.

KCG says the City of Aurora, Aurora Housing Authority, Adams County and the Colorado Division of Housing expressed support, and the city connected it with the police department's PAR program; an attorney opinion on the 10-year rule was attached to the application.
KCG reports over $1 billion of acquisitions and development nationally, more than 4,300 units and over 20 tax credit projects in nine states.

timeline.event: KCG signs purchase and sale agreement
CHFA announces 2024 Round Two awards, including Tiara Apartments
Existing HAP contract set to expire; financial closing targeted for the first half of 2025

open_questions: Whether KCG closed on the purchase, and the seller, price and date (Adams County records were not reachable for this review).
Whether the CHFA bonds closed and rehab started; the first-half-2025 closing target has passed with no public record.
Status of the RAD conversion and whether the expiring Moderate Rehabilitation HAP contract was extended in the meantime.
Whether the Aurora Housing Authority partnership and the Capital Magnet Fund loan were finalized.
Total development cost, equity investor and price, bond purchaser, CHFA affordability period; no public site plans or renderings were found.
